failure_pattern: The interior door handle sub-assembly breaks internally under ordinary opening force. The failed part is a plastic link or housing where the release cable attaches to the handle, a pivot pin or bell-crank, or the return-spring retainers. The handle then hangs loose and no longer pulls the latch cable. The door can still be opened with the exterior handle once the window is lowered. Failures come without warning, mostly on the driver's door but also on the front passenger and rear doors, between roughly 3,400 and 13,000 miles and within about the first year of ownership. Owners report failures on a second door, and replacement or swapped handles failing again. Two complaints say the door could not be opened from outside either (11757331 says the inside and outside handles both stopped working; 11759280 says the door would open neither way). These may involve the latch rather than the handle and are exceptions.

findings.text: Many independent owners describe the same failure: the interior handle breaks internally under normal use, goes loose, and the door cannot be opened from inside. Exiting requires lowering the window and using the exterior handle, or climbing across the cab.

Owners' descriptions, some citing dealer findings, point to the same parts. They describe a fractured plastic hinge pin or bell-crank (11761560), a broken plastic piece or connection where the cable attaches to the handle (11761814, 11752358, 11745636, 11692976), and a broken cable (11771154, 11767229). One owner quotes a dealer repair order: internal return springs disengaged from their retention points, which the dealer attributed to retainer design and material fatigue (11747995).
Failures happen at low mileage: about 3,429, 4,476, 4,700, 6,000, 6,300, 7,000, 7,055, 8,038, 8,800, 9,300, 10,000, about 11,000 and 13,000 miles. The dossier median is 6,000 miles.
The failure repeats on the same vehicle. Owners report a second door failing, a swapped handle breaking again, or a handle failing again right after repair.
Front passenger and rear door handles fail the same way, so the problem is not limited to one door.

Owners say dealers reported national backorders of the replacement assembly, one citing 1,600 units, and called the failure a known or common issue. One dealer provided a rental, citing safety. In one more case, an owner says the dealer had a second Tacoma with the same handle failure (11750131).
Entrapment has already happened in practice: a disabled owner could not get out and needed someone to open the door from outside.

Off-pattern or weaker complaints: one describes a smart-key or auto-lock fault and is unrelated (11725346). Two report the door would not open from outside either, which may be a latch fault rather than the handle (11757331, 11759280).

headline: 2025 Toyota Tacoma: interior door handle assemblies break in normal use at low mileage, so occupants cannot open the door from inside. Replacement parts are reported on national backorder and no recall covers the problem.
open_questions: Does the problem extend beyond the 2025 model year? The 2024 Tacoma has 4 complaints and is surging but has no PRR signal yet; the 2026 has 1 complaint. Does the same inner handle part number go on those years? Some owners also mention the 4Runner and Tundra, which has not been checked.
Are there Toyota warranty claim counts or a technical service bulletin for this assembly, and has a revised part been released? Owners report replacement handles failing again.
How many vehicles are waiting on backordered parts, and is Toyota offering any interim fix?
Does losing the interior release on a front door raise a compliance question under FMVSS 206 requirements for door locks and door retention components, or is this a safety-defect question only?
Are 11757331 and 11759280, which report that the door could not be opened from outside either, a separate latch failure?

provenance.note: Written by an AI (Claude) from public NHTSA complaint and recall data, and fact-checked against the cited complaints by a second AI. Not reviewed by a person. It describes what owners report; it is not a finding that a defect exists.

recalls.note: Shock absorber flange corrosion on 2024-2025 Tacoma.
2026 Mercedes GLA 250: an incorrectly installed Bowden cable can stop the door opening from inside. This is the same hazard, recalled even though only 10 vehicles were affected.
Toyota Prius rear door switch short circuit lets the door open unexpectedly. Different failure mode.

safety_risk: Occupants can be trapped. The way out through the affected door is to lower the window and reach the exterior handle, which needs electrical power for the window and the physical ability to reach outside. After a crash, fire, submersion or loss of power, an occupant could be delayed or unable to get out. Children in rear seats are especially at risk, and so are occupants with limited mobility: one disabled owner had to call for help to get out (11771763). Parts backorders leave affected trucks in service with the defect for weeks to months. No crashes, fires, injuries or deaths have been reported so far.
summary: I read all 53 complaints in the signal window. About 50 describe the same failure. An interior door release handle breaks inside the door during normal use. The handle goes loose or 'floppy' and no longer releases the latch, so that door cannot be opened from inside. Most reports are for the driver's door, with some for the front passenger and rear doors. In most cases the exterior handle still works. The theme is labelled 'rear door latch', but the real problem is the inner handle sub-assembly on any door, mostly the front doors. That mismatch probably explains why the automatic check marked 9 complaints off-theme and 9 unclear. Where owners give mileage, failures happened between about 3,400 and 13,000 miles. Dealers, as reported by owners, describe a fractured plastic part where the release cable attaches to the handle, a broken pivot pin or bell-crank, and return springs that came out of their retainers. Several owners had more than one door fail, or a replacement handle fail again. Many owners, reporting what dealers told them, say the part is on national backorder because of high demand, with one figure of 1,600 units. So vehicles are being driven for weeks or months with a door that cannot be opened from inside. Complaints rose steadily, from 2 a month in April and May 2026 to 12 in October 2026. The surge is very strong: 33 complaints in the last 3 months against 7.06 expected. The PRR is 33.8. No crash, fire, injury or tow has been reported. None of the 5 recalls for this vehicle covers door handles. The 2024 Tacoma has 4 complaints on this theme and is surging, but it has no PRR signal yet. The 2026 has 1 complaint. Whether the problem extends to other model years of this generation is a hypothesis that still needs checking.

theme.name: Rear door latch fails to open or close
